assessment.summary: CD274 (PD-L1) is a highly validated immuno-oncology target with exceptional structural, chemical, and clinical evidence. Five approved antibody drugs exist, over 1,700 ChEMBL IC50 entries are recorded, and 80 PDB structures including sub-angstrom resolution co-crystal structures confirm a well-characterised binding interface. The target is broadly considered high-druggability, though small-molecule engagement of the PD-1/PD-L1 interface remains challenging relative to antibody-based approaches.
evidence_gaps: Small-molecule druggability of the PD-1/PD-L1 protein-protein interaction interface is inherently difficult; most approved agents are monoclonal antibodies, and small-molecule inhibitors have not yet reached approval
Resistance mechanisms (e.g., CD274 amplification, alternative immune checkpoints) are not fully characterised and may limit therapeutic durability
Predictive biomarkers for patient stratification beyond PD-L1 expression level remain incompletely defined
Tissue-specific and isoform-specific biology (e.g., soluble PD-L1) is not fully captured in current structural or chemical datasets
Long-term safety profile and immune-related adverse events for newer agents (sugemalimab, cosibelimab) are still accumulating
